item.title: Please, Convert Your Files (properly)
item.description:
A tragedy I've seen many times: Someone renames a .png file to a .jpg file, and they think that their file was magically converted. Suddenly, they get thrown an error because the file isn't actually a JPG.

This is because you're only changing the name of the file extension. Sure, it might say “.jpg” right there, but all of the data in your image is still that of a PNG.

I'll admit that I've done the same thing tons of times when I was still learning how to use a computer. This is why I implore you to use something like VERT to convert your files properly and save yourself the headache of trying to figure out why your image isn't working as it should.

item.title: RSS
item.description:
Do you like RSS feeds? Do you want to make one for your website? No? Too bad.

First, what even is RSS?

RSS stands for Really Simple Syndication and it is a web feed that allows anyone to receive updates to websites using something called a feed reader.

This is an example of an RSS feed:

					
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" ?>
<rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom">
    <channel>
        <title>feed title</title>
        <description>posts from your-website.com</description>
        <link>https://your-website.com</link>
        <atom:link href="https://link-to-your-feed" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml" />
        <webMaster>email@domain.com (name)</webMaster>

        <!--Example Post-->
        <item>
		<title>post title</title>
		<link>https://your-website.com/yourpost.html</link>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">guid-here</guid>
        <description>
        Description Here
        </description>
		<pubDate>Day, dd Mon yyyy 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>  <!--Example Date: Thu, 29 Jun 2027 19:30:10 -0500-->
        <author>email@domain.com (name)</author>  
        </item>

    </channel>
</rss>

Everything is pretty self explanatory. You put the title in the <title> tags, the description in the <description> tags, and so on.

This format is very nice for website updates that just need a simple summary, but what if you want to include your whole article in one item for something like, say, a blogpost? That's where CDATA comes in.

What is CDATA?

CDATA stands for Character Data, and it allows you to include HTML markup inside of your items. Here's an example: 

					 
		<item>
		<title>post title</title>
		<link>https://your-website.com/yourpost.html</link>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">guid-here</guid>
        <description>
        <![CDATA[
        <p>This is a paragraph.</p>
        <p>This is another paragraph.</p>
        <p>You can put HTML markup inside of <strong>CDATA.</strong></p>
        ]]>
        You can also include a regular description.
        </description>
		<pubDate>Day, dd Mon yyyy 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>  <!--Example Date: Thu, 29 Jun 2027 19:30:10 +0300-->
        <author>email@domain.com (name)</author>  <!--This is optional.-->
        </item>

Here's a picture taken from Akregator that shows how the description would look:

You can also put images and links, but I'm too lazy to re-do the example.

The example file can be viewed here.

Feed Readers

Obviously, when you first open an RSS feed link, you only see a bunch of code. How do you see everything in an actually readable format? That's where feed readers come in.

A feed reader takes an RSS feed (usually in XML format) and turns it into something human-readable. I'll show you how to use one.

For this demonstration, I'm going to use Feedbro. First, you have to download Feedbro in your browser of choice. (I also recommend RSS Guard.)

Once you download Feedbro, click on its icon and then on the "Open Feed Reader" button at the top.


You'll see these icons in the top-left corner. Click on the one with the RSS logo to add a feed.


Once you click the "Add a New Feed" button, you will see this pop-up. Input the Feed URL and Title and then click Save.


The feed you added will now appear on the left panel. Congratulations, you've now set up your feed reader! You can add as many RSS feeds as you'd like using the same steps.

This post turned out a lot longer than I thought it would be. I hope this helps with your RSS needs!

item.title: This Page
item.description:
"Or more specifically, the Posts page."

This is something I've thought about, and then put off, just to think about it even more. It's the way I have my posts stored on my website.

I want to have my posts all on the same page, whether they be put under a details element or just all laid out there for you to scroll endlessly, but I would have to sacrifice a lot of the accessibility on mobile to do so.

My brain is weird. The way I have my posts laid out currently—with you having to go to a separate page for each post—makes me feel like I *have* to make each post long enough to be deserving of a whole entire page. Like it's some grand gesture. I want to be able to make shorter posts without my brain being weird about it, and this is a way that makes sense to me.

Sometimes, I just want to write about something mundane, like how I went to the grocery store and xyz happened, but I'm not going to write up a storm about it. Maybe it'll just be 3 or so sentences, and I'll say to myself "Come on, I'm not gonna dedicate a whole entire page to three sentences!" and then leave my journal to collect dust.

I could have separate pages dedicated to certain weeks, but what if I want to make longer posts back-to-back? That would be so much to scroll through! The same goes with if I were to just lay it out there.

But if I were to have every post be collapsible, I feel like it wouldn't work for a shorter post. You see "New post!" in the changelog just for it to be a single paragraph. Ugh. Or am I overthinking this?

Let me know your thoughts. I really have no idea on what to do.

item.title: Torrenting and Download Managers
item.description:
As you may know, I'm really into downloading random things on the internet and wasting my storage. I also like wasting my storage more efficiently, which has introduced me to the world of torrents and download managers, and I think it would be great if more people knew of them!

Let's start with my favourite: Torrenting.

What is torrenting?

When you download a file, you send a request to a central server, and that server sends you said file. Every download of that file goes through that server, and only that server, which puts strain on the connection.

What torrenting does instead, is that it downloads chunks of the file from other users' computers on the network and pieces them together. Imagine it as cutting your food into bite-sized pieces instead of downing the whole thing at once.

For torrenting, I recommend using qBittorrent. Please don't use uTorrent.

Main benefits of torrenting:

  1. Downloads are resumable. I find torrenting much more reliable at this, as resuming downloads on my browser results in the download failing 99% of the time.
  2. Faster download speeds! Torrents are very great for downloading large files which would otherwise take me several hours to download normally.
  3. It's decentralized. If your download gets stuck, you can continue downloading using another source.
  4. Files are very easy to find using search extensions or resources like Torrents-CSV or FMHY.

There are some downsides to all of this, though:

  1. People who are downloading/sharing the same file as you can see your IP.
  2. If you're torrenting something like a movie and you're living in a country that cares about copyright laws, like the US, you might also get a letter from your ISP telling you to stop.

Both of these issues can be avoided by using a VPN and binding your torrent client to it. I recommend Mullvad VPN, which costs 5 euros/month, and Cloudflare WARP, which is free.

Download Managers

If you don't want to go through all of that hassle just to get faster downloads, you can also use download managers. A download manager is a software made for, well, downloading files.

Main benefits of using a download manager:

  1. Download managers establish multiple connections to a server to achieve faster download speeds, and circumvent bandwidth limits.
  2. Like torrenting, download managers are more reliable at resuming downloads than browsers.
  3. Instead of being forced to go on a file host and having to go through a bunch of pages to download your files, your download manager will get the link for you using a Link Grabber.
  4. They give you the ability to do automatic actions upon completion, such as auto-unzipping bundles, putting your computer to sleep, etc.
  5. Download managers like IDM (paid) or JDownloader (free) have browser integrations that let you download files more easily.

Do keep in mind that the JDownloader website has downloads that contain adware on the frontpage. This link has the downloads that do not contain adware. I'll also add a debloating guide below if you've downloaded it.

Debloating JDownloader

Go to Settings (Ctrl+P) > Advanced Settings. In "Filter Settings", look up these phrases and click on the checkboxes in each result to disable it.

  1. oboom
  2. premium alert
  3. Donate
  4. Banner
  5. Special Deals

I hope this knowledge helps you as it has helped me. Keep in mind that this isn't *everything* about torrents and file managers, and I advise you to do your own research. Make sure to use an adblocker and to scan your files for viruses, too!

item.title: Cold Brew (Tea)
item.description:
"Let's all love cold brew."

Today, I made some green tea. It tasted absolutely horrible, because I took too long to take the tea bag out before it started getting bitter. I thought to myself, "Why did I even make this if I could've just cold brewed it and saved myself the embarrassment?" In fact, I was so angry that I started writing a post about why you should cold brew your tea.

So, first things first, what is cold brewing? Cold brewing is when you brew your tea (or coffee) in cold water. It's much gentler than brewing it hot, because it extracts the flavour from the tea over the course of several hours. This greatly reduces the risk of your tea turning out bitter, and I find it has a better taste than making it with hot water.

Okay, I know that most people aren't going to wait 8 or 24 or however many hours *just* so they can drink some tea, but hear me out. I have a list of benefits of cold brewing your tea instead of just brewing it regularly:

  1. It's incredibly easy. Just put your tea and water in a bottle and leave it overnight, and the next day you'll have some tea ready to go!
  2. It's a very good method for making large batches of tea. I usually do a liter of it, but you can do much, much more.
  3. As I've said before, it's much less bitter, and even tastes sweeter. Sometimes you don't even have to add sweetener!
  4. I find it's much better than brewing it regularly when it comes to adding fruits to your tea, as it also extracts the flavours of the fruit more gently.

I really do encourage that you try cold brewing your tea if you've never tried it before. You can even just put a tea bag in a cup of water, leave it on the counter overnight, add a sweetener of choice, and try it out! If you like it, that's great! If you don't, that's fine too! I hope this helps somebody find out the magic of cold brewing, haha.

item.title: Windows 11 Out of the Box
item.description:
"I tried out a fresh install of Windows 11 and hated it."

I'm among one of the many people who moved to Linux because, well, Windows 11 just sucks. The forced updates, the entire Recall thing, Copilot being forced onto you every single second of your life, and many other things.

I must say that my Windows 11 experience wasn't *that* awful. Why? Because I had to cake on 50 system tweaks just so my system could be usable, and I don't think I have to say that you shouldn't have to do that.

I really enjoy playing around with virtual machines, so I figured, why not try a fresh install of Windows 11? It'd be interesting to see just how different it is from my previous setup.

I'm not going to comment on the speed, since I allocated only 5 GB of RAM to my VM, which Windows eats for breakfast, but I can safely say everything else was awful.

First things first, it tried to force me to connect a Microsoft account, and when I managed to bypass that, I was IMMEDIATELY bombarded with ads on the Start menu. Who the fuck puts ads in a paid operating software? And the taskbar has these "widgets" that I do not care about in any way, and, of course, Copilot is shoved in my face.

I geniunely can't recommend Chris Titus' Winutil enough. I would've gone crazy trying to disable all of the junk on the taskbar without this utility. Though, I must tell you to please not run any command you see on the internet if you don't know what it does.

Something else I noticed is that Notepad has Copilot, and it's locked behind a subscription? I don't understand who exactly would need AI inside of Notepad, and who would need it so badly that they'd pay for it. It also requires you to sign into a Microsoft account, which is nice.

That aside, it does what you expect an operating software to do. That's until the newest update breaks something you're using, like Localhost, or Windows Recovery.

By the way, and this is just my opinion, I think File Explorer sucks. Check out something like Q-Dir or Directory Opus obtained through (cough) legal methods if you'd like an alternative.

I'm not going to be insufferable and call you a moron for using Windows and that you must switch to Linux immediately, but if you've never used Linux before, please give it a chance. Try out a distribution on something like VirtualBox (make sure to have virtualization enabled virst) and see if you like it!

If you don't know which of the many distributions to choose, check out Linux Mint or Pop!_OS. (Please don't let anybody convince you to use Arch as your first distro.) Even better, go on Distro Chooser and see which of the results interests you the most.

item.title: Misogyny in Metal Gear Solid
item.description:
Let me preface: I love Metal Gear Solid. I feel like I have to say this given how Metal Gear Solid fans are.

When I got into Metal Gear Solid, I saw a very glaring issue, which was the misogyny that hits you in the face in every game. Whether it be every female character being sexualized to hell and back (like with Quiet) or being sidelined or just straight up killed (EVA, Naomi, Strangelove, etc.)

It started with MGS1, with the camera zooming onto Meryl's ass, and Solid Snake harassing her, and whatever else that I blocked out of my memory, and then MGS2, with the "easter eggs" featuring Japanese adult actresses, which made me question if it was worth it to continue onto the next games, and I think I reached my breaking point when I saw Quiet.

She has to breathe through her skin, which forces her to wear basically nothing.. and she doesn't talk (Yes, I know why she doesn't talk, but still.) And there have been more scenes where they zoom onto her chest than I could count.

You could say the constant sexualisation was just MGS being a product of its time, but it still makes my skin crawl. It also doesn't help that (most of) the people in the fanbase will chalk up what you say to pure stupidity or try to invalidate your take by mentioning The Boss, and while I admit that she's a solid character, but that doesn't take away from the misogynistic writing in the games.

I've seen people be called slurs, be sent death threats, and get the most vicious hate I've witnessed at the hands of MGS fans just for having the same takes as I. I don't think I should be told "This is why females should've never joined the gaming community" just for saying a franchise has misogynistic writing.

These are only a few examples. I haven't touched MGS in months so I don't remember much else. If anybody reading this has some thoughts on this, feel free to reach out.

item.title: 100 Webmaster Questions
item.description:
"I was bored, so I joined in on the fun."

Find the blank here.

1. Please introduce yourself.
I'm Saif, I really like pages with a lot of links. I like collecting pamphlets from tech stores.
2. How long have you been making websites?
I've been making websites since 2023.
3. And what got you into the hobby?
An ex-friend of mine had a really nice Neocities page.
4. What kind of website are you most interested in?
Personal websites and wikis.
5. What's your workflow? Do you plan your websites out thoroughly or do you come up with the design as you go along?
I make things up as I go. I'm not one for planning.
6. Please link to your biggest inspirations.
Wikipedia and the belated txti.
7. What's your favourite part about making websites?
Getting it to look how I want it to.
8. And the thing you struggle with the most?
Coming up with new ideas.
9. Do you keep the same layout on all of your pages? Or do you use different ones?
I keep the same layout across all pages. I don't really have any layout ideas either way.
10. How confident are you with CSS?
Is "ehhhhhhh" a valid answer?
11. Do you know how to correctly use <dl>?
Yes.
12. What is your favourite HTML element?
I'm a huge fan of ul.
13. If you're making a new web page from scratch, what is the first thing you do?
Hide ASCII art of a random character inside of a comment.
14. Do you know JavaScript?
Not as much as I'd like to.
15. How about PHP?
Nope.
16. Does your website have a theme that you stick to?
You could say I'm a fan of black text on a white background.
17. Are you more focused on content or design?
Content matters more to me.
18. Do you own a domain name? If not, would you ever want to?
Sadly, I don't have domain money, so no.
19. What do you think of nostalgia-focused or "retro" websites?
I think they're nice, though I've noticed that 99% of them are Windows XP themed.
20. Is your HTML valid? Do you even check?
No....
21. What are your opinion on buttons and banners?
I really like buttons, especially on personal websites. I don't think I've seen many banners, though.
22. What do you think of button walls in particular?
They're nice, but those with a bunch of flashing buttons next to each other really suck. Sucks even harder when there's no warning.
23. If you started over again, would you make something similar or completely different?
I'd probably make the same thing.
24. Are you envious of other people's websites?
No, but there are some that I get inspired by.
25. What text editor do you use?
I use Kate.
26. Why do you use that one?
I got tired of VSCode pushing me to use Copilot, and I lke free and open source software.
27. Do you host your image files on your web server, or on another host?
I host my image files directly on Nekoweb.
28. This might not be relevant to you, but what's your opinion on the Neocities vs. Nekoweb debate?
I don't care for it.
29. How much server space would you estimate your main website takes up?
Around 8 MB.
30. Do you keep local backups of your files?
I code my website locally and then upload it to Nekoweb. When I want to make a huge change I'll make a copy of whatever I'm editing.
31. Do you prefer simple or highly visual websites?
I like both, but I have a specific kind of hatred for websites with 500 floating images that cover up the main content.
32. Do you stick to certain colours? Do you do that on purpose, or is it your subconscious?
I enjoy grayscale with pops of colour. I don't really pay attention to it.
33. Have you ever thought about quitting? Why?
No, making my website brings me joy.
34. Do you have many webmaster friends, or is it a solitary hobby?
Depends on your definition of "friend." I'd say I've made quite a few.
35. Do people in your real life know about your website?
I think, like, 4 people know?
36. Do you update your website very often? How often is "very often"?
I used to update my website daily after my move to Nekoweb, but I've calmed down in recent times.
37. And the overall design, do you change that much? Why or why not?
No. Again, I don't have any reason to change my design.
38. Is your website more you-focused, hobby-focused, or outside world-focused?
I'd say it's me-focused and a little hobby-focused.
39. Do you do web design professionally?
God, no.
40. If not, would you like to? And if you're comfortable answering, what do you do for work?
I can't say I'm into the idea of turning my hobby into a profession, it sounds like a surefire way to start hating it. Unfortunately, I am unemployed.
41. Do you communicate with people by email very much?
Yes! I love emails more than anything. Please email me.
42. Some people reject social media and use websites as a replacement. Do you keep social media outside of your website?
Yes. I mostly just lurk on social media either way.
43. How about instant messengers? Do you use a mainstream one like Discord or Telegram? Or something like Matrix? Do you avoid them?
I use telegram mostly for downloading paid procreate brushes because, like, who do you think you are? I also use Discord and I hate it.
44. Do you listen to music while you work on websites? If so, what kinds of artists?
According to the Music Statistics Site, I've listened to Ecstatic Vibrations, Totally Transcendent by Sea Power 340 times while making and editing this website.
45. Do you keep everything you make on one website, or do you have more than one?
I keep everything on one website.
46. On a similar note, do you keep to one topic on your site, or many?
I don't think I could ever focus on only one single topic.
47. Do you present your real self, or at least try? Or do you construct a persona on purpose?
I try to be as open as I can.
48. Have you ever made a good friend thanks to your website?
Yes.
49. Are you happy with the way HTML and CSS currently work?
I have a few grievances, but I'm satisfied.
50. What are practices that you think people should avoid?
MEDIA AUTOPLAY. And comments in the source code giving me shit for snooping around.
51. What about under-utilised practices, or things you think people should do more?
People should use the details element more. I love it.
52. Do you use a lot of semantic HTML? Or are you guilty of generic structure?
I try to use semantic HTML as much as I can.
53. Do you consider different browsers?
I tried using Helium (chromium browser) once. It was nice save for the fact there's no vertical tabs.
54. Speaking of, what's your preferred browser? Convince your readers why they should use it.
Librewolf. It has vertical tabs and none of the AI bullshit that Firefox has. Who doesn't like that?
55. And what OS are you on?
I use Linux Mint.
56. Do you have a strong opinion on that, or do you just happen to use it?
I got tired of Microsoft and auto updates as one does and made the switch. It also doesn't make my laptop heat up to 99 degrees Celsius.
57. Are your websites mobile-friendly?
Yes.
58. What are your thoughts on autoplay?
I hate it with every cell in my body.
59. What are your thoughts on webrings? Are you in any?
I'm in a few webrings. Haven't found more to join though...
60. Do you have any web shrines? What do you like to see in that sort of page?
I wish I could make one, but I lack the brainpower to do so. I love the web shrines I come across while surfing the web, though. I like the makesweet gifs some of them have.
61. Are your websites "cliche", in your opinion?
I don't think so?'
62. What is your ideal website? Are you striving for that, or for something else?
A massive resources page. Art galleries are cool too.
63. Are you an artist? Do you draw or design your own assets?
I'd consider myself an artist, though I haven't been drawing much lately. I drew my own button and favicon.
64. What are your favourite resource sites?
FMHY and The Internet Archive.
65. Is there a habit you just can't get away from no matter how hard you try?
Inline CSS...
66. What's your biggest advice for a new webmaster?
Learn CSS selectors and Flexbox. Use Inspect Element on sites you like the look of.
67. Do you keep all your styling in CSS? Or do you hard-code some?
I do a bit of both.
68. What do you think of frameset layouts?
Huh, I thought framesets were deprecated... I do enjoy iframes, though.
69. How about table-based layouts?
Those are nice.
70. Do you subscribe to the ideas of "one-column", "two-column" and "three-column" layouts? Do you use any of these?
I don't really care for them. I suppose I like one-column layouts?
71. Do you spend longer on the HTML or the CSS?
Definitely the CSS.
72. Have you ever made a page with no CSS? It's useful for your thoughts.
Yeah.
73. Do you ever find yourself making layouts with nothing to put on them? Or do you only make layouts when the need arises?
I make layouts when the need arises.
74. Would you consider yourself a beginner? Or advanced? Somewhere in the middle?
I'd say I'm a beginner.
75. Do you have a habit of looking at the source code of websites you visit?
Of course.
76. How did YOU learn how to make websites?
Looking things up when something goes wrong and looking at other websites' source code.
77. Do you ever force elements to do things they're not supposed to?
I'm an upstanding member of society, so no.
78. Thoughts on floating elements?
They're useful.
79. When you're sizing stuff, what do you use first? Do you use px, em, %, or something else?
em or px depending on the weather.
80. Do you have a favourite font?
Times New Roman all the way.
81. Would you run a website with another person? How would that work?
Sure! It sounds fun.

item.title: English
item.description:
"A little incoherent."

I'm sure you know that English is not my first language, Arabic is, and that's why my english is not that good. You'd expect that I would be better at speaking Arabic, but no. My Arabic is *much* poorer than my English.

I had to teach myself English because, well, how would I hope to make friends on the internet if I don't know how to speak English? One of the consequences is that I get worse and worse at speaking Arabic every day. Hell, even my friends think I'm a foreigner.

It makes me a little sad. It's as if I've been disconnected from who I am, and where I come from. I could tell you right now that I speak Arabic, and I'd be right, but sometimes it feels like I'm lying. That it's not *actually* my mother tongue.

I learned English through watching YouTube videos. I know that it's great that I learned an entire language by myself, but I still feel like I regret it. I feel like I'm being stripped of something inherent to me, day by day. Maybe one day it'll be completely gone? I hope not.

Though, if I never learned English, what friends would I have?

item.title: Homosexuality, Religion, and Egypt
item.description:
"As you can tell, I am quite the patriot. Warning for homophobia and religious talk."

Since the first grade, I've known that I'm in some way queer. I thought that it was quite the normal thing, that how could anybody possibly be upset at you for realising who you truly are?

Obviously, I was wrong. I *attempted* to come out to my mother shortly after, and was only told that it's wrong to think like that. That I'm misguided and that people like that will go to hell.

I was nothing short of devastated. I had always been the good religious girl my family wanted me to be, and now my own religion rejects me? Why must I be sentenced to eternal damnation just for knowing who I am? Why does the whole world hate me for it?

Since then, whenever I ask my mother for anything, she always makes sure to tell me that "those people" are wrong and will go to hell if they don't repent. Like she knows something. I always smile and nod because I don't have the luxury of being my true self. I will never be able to move out and transition and live the life I want, it's just not what my future holds.

I've seen how we are treated by the Egyptian government. They think we're animals that don't deserve to live. They'll throw you in a cell and leave you to rot. There's not one day where I don't mourn Sarah Hegazi.

Needless to say, that severed the connection I had felt with my religion. Why should I have to follow a religion that wants me dead? Why did God create me just to tell me that I'm going to hell no matter what? Is it even worth it to do anything, knowing I'll never be who I want to be? That I'll actively be punished for it?

Why should I have to love the country that hates me? That persecutes people like me without batting an eye? That views me as a "national security threat"?

I still want to have hope for what the future holds. Who knows how long everything will keep being like this? I'd like to think everything will get better despite it all.

item.title: Journaling and This Website
item.description:
"This one is quite personal. Warning: I talk about my experiences with paranoia here."

Earlier I was thinking about my website, and my journal, and I asked myself: Why did I even make a journal? I came to the conclusion that it was because I wanted to be seen, but I also realised that's the reason I made this whole website in the first place. Yeah, the first paragraph *does* say that I made this website because I got tired of linktrees and strawpages and whatever other websites are out there, but this is more the overall reason why I made this website.

Obviously I'm not going to write out my whole life story here, but to put it simply I had a few events during my childhood that ended up with me becoming quite the asocial (and paranoid) person. I still am, but I've been trying hard to remedy it.

I couldn't talk to people without thinking to myself, "What if they're friends with me as some kind of sick inside joke?" or, "What if, someday, I'm going to wake up and all of my friends will just be gone? What's the point of having friends, then?" I was afraid to even be *perceived* by people I didn't know. That's how bad it was!

I don't want to be stuck in a friendless limbo, nobody does. That's why I made this website in the first place, why I started talking to other people more. Hell, it's the reason why I even started to e-mail people and tell them how much I love their website, or their art, or really anything!

It's also why I'm here writing this post for whoever might read it... I just want to better myself.

item.title: AI
item.description:
"About time I posted an AI rant! I really do hate it."

I know it's been said many times by many different people, but I truly do hate how AI has been taking over the internet. Everywhere I go I see something about a "new AI feature" or I get a notification begging me to go try XYZ websites AI chatbot. Hell, even W3schools has an "AI helper" now.

Every new device has AI built-in nowadays. I can't even take a screenshot on my phone without being told to edit it using AI! I have to go out of my way to disable Copilot every time I open my laptop.

Remember Windows Recall? The thing that screenshots EVERYTHING on your desktop, even your passwords and personal info? You could tell me: Saif, we've been surveilled before the AI boom ever happened, don't be naive. Yes, but it still scares me. Privacy is like a fever dream now.

Every day I see more and more people use AI to think for them. It's even happening to my family! My classmates! I've seen my own mother use Gemini to look things up instead of just using a search engine. I've seen my classmates use ChatGPT to look up the simplest questions ever. And for what? So we can ruin the environment faster? So we can make ourselves dumber day by day? It's just so horrifying to watch.

I've used Firefox ever since I've known how to use a computer. Can you imagine how I felt when I saw "try our new AI chatbot" pop up after I updated it? I feel like I'm going crazy.

I could bring up a billion more reasons as to why I hate AI. AI being used for warfare, xAI taking water and clean air away from black families in Memphis, AI being used to bully artists and to steal and deface their work... Can you tell I don't like AI?

item.title: Autoplay
item.description:
"Media autoplay (and why I hate it with my entire being.) Happy October!"

There are many things I love about making and looking at websites. I love having something that is uniquely mine, and I love seeing websites where you can feel every bit of soul the author(s) put into them. I love the freedom that it gives you. You can basically do anything!

But there's one thing I absolutely cannot get myself to like no matter how hard I try. Autoplay. First of all, it's not accessible. Second of all, why are you trying to jump scare me via audio file? I understand wanting people to listen to songs you like. I really do. But there HAS to be another way to do that, no?

Something that's even worse is when there's autoplay but no way to make it stop playing. I sometimes use a screen reader while I browse, and having an audio on autoplay and not being able to pause it is terrible. I imagine it must be terrible for others too.

And don't get me started on video autoplay. If I didn't know of the existence of pop-up blockers I probably would've lost my mind a long time ago. I could write an entire book about how much I hate video autoplay. (Also, who in their right mind thought it was a good idea to have video autoplay automatically enabled on YouTube?)

At the end of the day, you can do whatever you want with your website. I'm not going to hover over people and tell them not to put autoplay on their websites. Who am I to do that? But PLEASE at least put a warning that your website has autoplay on it... Thanks.
